segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: To speak.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Do you remember how to say to speak? It begins with a silent h.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Hablar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Hablar, good. And what is I speak or I'm speaking?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Hablo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Hablo,

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: good. And what was to sleep, or to be dormant let's say?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Dormir.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Dormir. And how do you say I sleep?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Duermo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. We said also that you can get the additional meaning of I fall asleep by saying I sleep myself.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Me duermo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Me duermo, good. To eat was?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Comer.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Comer, good. So, I eat or I'm eating is?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Como.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Como. So here the o doesn't split, good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: To have breakfast. To have breakfast, we don't say in Spanish to have breakfast, we have a verb to breakfast, let's say. And the verb to breakfast is desayunar, desayunar.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Desayunar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Breakfast and desayunar are direct translations of each other in fact. I don't know if you noticed that in English, breakfast is break fast. When we have breakfast we break the fast. And in Spanish, des is like un-, ayunar is to fast. So, to unfast. So, desayunar is like to unfast, to breakfast. Desayunar.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Desayunar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: To have breakfast. I am having breakfast, or I have breakfast?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Desayuno.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Desayuno. And desayuno is also the noun, el desayuno is the breakfast.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: What was to wait or to hope?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Desperate is related, because again we have this des, like in desayunar, which is like un-hoped or unhopeful is to be desperate. So, to wait or to hope?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Esperar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good, esperar, good. What is I wait, or I'm waiting, or I hope and or I'm hoping?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Espero.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Espero. So, we've been giving the verbs two translations in the present tense: I speak or I'm speaking, I go or I'm going, I wait or I'm waiting.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: This is because this -ing tense in English, we really overuse it.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: For example, we use this -ing in English to refer to the future. He's doing it tomorrow, whereas in Spanish we just use the present tense with that future context: lo hace mañana.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Which is why we need to give both translations for hace, for example. He makes or does, or he's making or doing. And we translate hablo as I speak and I'm speaking.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: But this doesn't mean that I'm speaking doesn't exist.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: It does exist, but we use it in Spanish only when we want to show what we are doing right now in this moment.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, beginning this structure, I am speaking, this I am, do you think you would choose ser for characteristics, or do you think you would choose estar for states?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Well, it's it's a state, so estoy.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good, we will use estar because of course what we are doing is a state. So, we'll always use estar with these structures. So, the first part of this sentence is estoy.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now to get speaking, -ing from to speak, we take off -ar and we add -ando, -ando, and we get hablando.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Hablando.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, I'm speaking?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estoy hablando.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Estoy hablando, good. So, maybe somebody interrupts you and you won't say hablo, you would say estoy hablando.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you say I am waiting, and you mean right now, right now, I'm waiting here, I'm waiting here?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estoy esperando aquí.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Estoy esperando aquí, good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, you could say espero aquí, maybe it would sound a little more like I'll wait here, rather than I am waiting here, but both are fine. In many situations both are fine and there will be just a slight change in meaning: espero aquí, estoy esperando aquí.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: What you can't do is say I'm meeting with her tomorrow, uh? The -ing, you need to use it just for what you're doing right now.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, how was to speak?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Hablar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And how would you say I speak or I'm speaking?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Hablo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Hablo. And what was to prepare, if you forgot it you can go from preparation?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Preparación, preparar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And I prepare or I'm preparing?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Preparo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So, how would you say I am preparing it tomorrow?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo preparo mañana.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Lo preparo mañana. So, if we want to show, if we want to emphasize that we're doing something right now, I am preparing, firstly if we divide that up into two bits: I am, preparing.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estoy.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Estoy, good. Preparar becomes?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Preparando.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So, how would you say I am preparing?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estoy preparando.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Estoy preparando, good. So, that's if you want to say I'm preparing it right now, you can use this structure.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, how would you say I am preparing it?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo estoy preparando.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Lo estoy preparando or estoy preparándolo. Even though it's a changed verb here, we can have the lo after -ando. Estoy preparándolo or lo estoy preparando.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We said that to have breakfast was desayunar, desayunar.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, how would you say we are having breakfast, and you mean right now?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estamos desayunando.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: -ando, good. Estamos desayunando. So, for -ar verbs we take off the -ar and we put -ando and we get this tense to show what we're doing right now. And we're not going to use it as we do in English, I'm finding out tomorrow, um I'm doing it next week, I'm preparing it later. How would you say I'm preparing it later?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estoy preparando...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: This is not how we use it. So, in Spanish we only use it to describe what we're doing right now, ah? Right, so. So, this is why we're giving preparo, for example, the translation of both I prepare and I'm preparing, so that when we want to say things like I'm preparing it later we don't go to estoy preparando.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo preparo más tarde.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Lo preparo más tarde, good. But if you wanted to give the meaning of I'm preparing it right now, how would you say it?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Estoy preparándolo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Estoy preparándolo or lo estoy preparando. And there you get the meaning of of right now, in this moment. Good. So, for -ar verbs we're taking off the -ar and we're putting -ando to get this -ing. For -er/-ir verbs, we take off the -er or the -ir and we put on -iendo, -iendo, i-e-n-d-o to get this -ing form.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So, how would you get eating from to eat? How would eating be from comer?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Comiendo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. So, how would you say I'm eating and you mean right now?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Comien- estoy comiendo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Estoy comiendo, good, I am eating. And how would you say he is eating or she is eating or you formal?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Está comiendo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good, está comiendo. So, maybe somebody calls you and they say can I speak to Pablo and you say está comiendo, you mean right now. What was to sell? You can think of vending machine.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Vender.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vender, good. How would you say they sell it, they sell it?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Venden, so it's lo venden.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Lo venden, good. How would you say they're selling it tomorrow, or they will sell it tomorrow?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Lo venden mañana.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Lo venden mañana, good. Now, if you want to say they're selling it right now and you want to give that meaning right now, how would it be?

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Están vendiéndolo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Están vendiéndolo or lo están vendiendo, good.
